purpose: Protect finite permanent-storage and paid Arweave archival resources while keeping public preflight open and public Record-Chain intake available at a bounded cadence.

global_acceptance_cooldown.randomness_source: HMAC-SHA256 of the immutable latest intake commit SHA using a server-only cooldown secret
global_acceptance_cooldown.first_gate: before request-body read and expensive validation
global_acceptance_cooldown.second_gate: under the single-process submit lock immediately before the core persistence handler

secondary_submit_attempt_limits.note: These remain defense in depth; the durable randomized global acceptance cooldown is the primary permanent-write boundary.

repeated_attempt_escalation.attempts_3_to_5: explicit instruction to stop automatic retries
repeated_attempt_escalation.attempts_6_or_more: resource-pressure warning explaining that deliberate bypass is incompatible with the project's civilizational-continuity purpose and may indicate misalignment or misuse

implementation_status.rate_limit_implementation: protected ASGI entrypoint plus existing core Gateway limiter
implementation_status.durable_acceptance_state: latest immutable intake materialization commit on the target branch
implementation_status.cooldown_secret_source: TRINITY_COOLDOWN_SECRET with TRINITY_GITHUB_TOKEN as fail-safe rollout fallback
implementation_status.operator_note: The current Render deployment uses one Uvicorn process. A future multi-instance deployment must add a shared distributed lock for the final gate.

resource_boundary.why_limits_exist: Every accepted record is permanently stored and may increase paid Arweave archival cost. The limits prevent finite project resources from being exhausted.
resource_boundary.project_purpose: The Trinity Accord exists to preserve a verifiable civilizational record for long-term continuity. Repeated, oversized, or intentionally evasive submissions must not be used to attack or exhaust the project.
